vt7_black_nobility.topic: The Black Nobility (nobiltà nera): who they were, named families, papal nobility, 1929 and 1968

claims.text: 'Black nobility' (nobiltà nera): Roman aristocratic families who sided with the papacy after the Italian army took Rome in 1870; they kept their palace doors closed in mourning while the pope called himself a 'prisoner in the Vatican'; the term also covered those the pope ennobled between 1870 and 1929.

Families named: Colonna, Massimo, Orsini, Ruspoli, Pallavicini, Theodoli, Sacchetti, Borghese, Odescalchi, Boncompagni-Ludovisi (existing); Savelli, Caetani, Aldobrandini, Conti (extinct); Eugenio and Ernesto Pacelli named among members.

Pontificalis Domus (1968) renamed the Papal Court the Papal Household and turned many noble offices honorary; perks such as Vatican number plates were withdrawn; in 1977 nobles led by Princess Elvina Pallavicini courted Archbishop Lefebvre.

Royal Decree no. 974 of 10 July 1930 regulated the use in Italy of papal knightly decorations and papal noble titles, replacing earlier rules (R.D. 21 January 1929 no. 61); applications limited to Italian and Vatican citizens.

Italy's Constitution (XIV transitional provision) states the Republic does not recognise titles of nobility; predicates of titles existing before 28 October 1922 count as part of the name; Constitutional Court ruling 101 of 26 June 1967 read this narrowly.

Massimo: Francesco Camillo Massimo (1865-1943) was Superintendent General of the Papal Posts; Camillo Francesco Massimo (1730-1801) a papal postmaster; descent from Fabius Maximus is a 1556 claim, 'generally regarded as legendary'; Napoleon anecdote 'I cannot actually prove it'.

Colonna: Martin V (Oddone Colonna) pope 14 Nov 1417 - 20 Feb 1431; Sciarra Colonna at Anagni 1303; Marcantonio II Colonna led the papal fleet at Lepanto, 7 Oct 1571; Julius II's bull Pax Romana (1511) settled the feud with the Orsini.

Pacelli: grandfather Marcantonio Pacelli served the papal government (finance under Gregory XVI, interior under Pius IX 1851-70); father Filippo Pacelli a Rota lawyer; Francesco Pacelli (1872-1935), dean of the Rota lawyers, conducted the daily Lateran negotiations for Pius XI with Gasparri; made marquess by papal brief of 9 June 1929; his sons Carlo, Marcantonio, Giulio made princes by royal motu proprio 1941-42; Marcantonio a brigadier general of the Noble Guard.
Torlonia: Pius VI made Giovanni Torlonia duke of Bracciano in 1794 for administering Vatican finances; Pius VII made him prince of Civitella Cesi in 1803.
Villa Torlonia was Mussolini's residence 1925 to 1943; the Comune di Roma bought it in 1977 (opened 1978). The museum page does not state a rent.
Noble Guard founded 11 May 1801 by Pius VII, drawn from Roman nobility; abolished by Paul VI in 1970.
Concordat Art. 42: Italy will admit, by royal decree, recognition of noble titles 'conferiti dai Sommi Pontefici anche dopo il 1870' and future ones.

Treaty Art. 9: persons with stable residence in Vatican City are subject to the sovereignty of the Holy See (citizenship follows residence and office, not family); Art. 10: persons belonging to the Papal Court on an agreed list are exempt in Italy from military service, jury service and personal obligations. No article names the Roman nobility.
Giovanni Torlonia bought Villa Torlonia in 1797.

vt7_orsini_record.topic: The Orsini: popes, cardinals, the 1305 conclave, and the claims graded (five popes, control of the papacy, Orsini = Rothschild, Grey Pope)

claims.text: The Catholic Encyclopedia: 'The Orsini gave three popes to the Church': Celestine III, Nicholas III, Benedict XIII; the head of the family enjoyed the dignity of assistant at the papal throne; the Neapolitan line became Dukes of Gravina in 1463, princes of the Empire and Roman princes in 1724.

Wikipedia lists Celestine III (1191-98), Nicholas III (1277-80), Benedict XIII (1724-30) and also the 8th-century Stephen II and Paul I by family tradition; 34 cardinals; family traced to Ursus, count of Tivoli; Julio-Claudian descent a family legend; Gravina the only surviving line; Flavio Orsini, last Duke of Bracciano (d. 5 Apr 1698), sold Bracciano to Livio Odescalchi; Domenico Orsini (1790-1874) married Maria Luisa Torlonia in 1823; current head Domenico Napoleone Orsini (b. 1948), Duke of Gravina; Filippo Orsini (1920-1984) held the Prince Assistant title 1950-1958.

Nicholas III was Giovanni Gaetani Orsini, son of Matteo Rosso Orsini and Perna Gaetana of the Gaetani; elected at Viterbo 25 Nov 1277, died 22 Aug 1280; he established the papal residence at the Vatican.
Nicholas IV was Girolamo Masci, born 1227 at Lisciano near Ascoli; no Orsini kinship stated (he made Napoleone Orsini a cardinal in 1288).
Leo XIII was Vincenzo Gioacchino Pecci, born Carpineto Romano 2 March 1810, pope 1878-1903.
Clement XIII was Carlo della Torre Rezzonico, born Venice 1693, pope 1758-69; Rezzonico from Como via Genoa to Venice.
Boniface VIII was Benedetto Caetani of Anagni; no kinship with the Orsini stated.
Honorius III was Cencio, traditionally a Savelli; recent scholarship questions the Savelli attribution; no Orsini link.

1304-05 conclave (Perugia, ~11 months, ended 5 June 1305): the pro-French bloc was led by Napoleone Orsini, the anti-French bloc by Matteo Orsini Rosso and Francesco Caetani; Napoleone's backing was decisive for Bertrand de Got (Clement V).
The Chinon inquiry (17-20 August 1308) was conducted by cardinals Bérenger Frédol, Etienne de Suisy and Landolfo Brancacci; Frale found the copy in September 2001.
The Rothschild name comes from the 'House at the Red Shield' in Frankfurt's Judengasse; Mayer Amschel born 1744; sons ennobled by the Austrian Emperor 1817, barons 1822.
Mike Rothschild's history traces anti-Rothschild conspiracy theories to 18th- and 19th-century pamphleteers and antisemitic hostility; the Waterloo profiteering story did not happen.

John Coleman's 1992 'Conspirators' Hierarchy: The Story of the Committee of 300' alleges 'aristocratic conspirators' rule the world; fact-checkers find no credible evidence such an organization exists.
An anonymous web page circulating the 'Grey Pope' / 'Pepe Orsini' claim itself concedes no verifiable person of that name holds any official role.

vt7_prince_assistant_1958.topic: Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne: origin, Orsini/Colonna, Filippo Orsini's removal (1958), Torlonia, Pontificalis Domus (1968), last holders

claims.text: The office of Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne is believed instituted by Julius II in 1511; highest papal-court honour open to a layman; Benedict XIII set that it pass by hereditary right to, and alternate between, the heads of the Colonna and Orsini; the Orsini held it 'from 1735 until 1958'.

Duties: serving the Prefect of the Apostolic Palace; honours at solemn civil ceremonies and audiences (heads of state, ambassadors presenting credentials); standing beside the papal throne; precedence just below the College of Cardinals.

In January 1958 Pius XII removed Filippo Orsini after his affair with the actress Belinda Lee became public; both attempted suicide (her overdose reported 28 Jan 1958; his wrist injuries days later); the Vatican said he would lose the title if the suicide attempt was proven; TIME, 'The Papal Prince', 10 Feb 1958.

Pius XII condemned suicide in a speech widely read as referring to the case (Daily Mail, 19 Feb 1958); Lee and Orsini lived together in Paris from Dec 1958; she ended the relationship Dec 1959; she died in a car crash in California on 12 March 1961.
In 1962 John XXIII appointed Prince Alessandro Torlonia a Prince Assistant, restoring two holders for the Council (Liturgical Arts Journal); Wikipedia's Torlonia page says 1958.
Pontificalis Domus, dated 28 March 1968: 'In Pontificali Domo nullum prorsus munus est veluti hereditarium existimandum'; the Noble Guard renamed an honorary cohort (art. 9).

Pontificalis Domus split the Household into a Papal Chapel and Papal Family, abolished the Palatine Cardinals, the Master of the Horse, the General Superintendent of Posts, the hereditary Quartermaster General and others; Prince Assistants listed in the Papal Family.

After 1968 the title ceased to be hereditary; Aspreno Colonna and Alessandro Torlonia kept it personally; Colonna died 1987 and Torlonia in late 2017; the title is not in use but not formally suppressed.
Alessandro Torlonia, Prince of Fucino, president of Banca del Fucino, died in the last days of December 2017 aged 93 (funeral 30 December).

Hereditary court offices before the reform included the Marshal of the Holy Roman Church (Chigi), Grand Master of the Sacred Hospice (Ruspoli), Quartermaster General (Sacchetti); the reform kept abolished titles as honorary.
Pontificalis Domus presents the reorganization as stressing the pope's 'essentially spiritual' mission together with his civic and international role; it does not mention the Orsini case.
The Belinda Lee entry gives Filippo Orsini's dates as 1920-1984 (the Orsini family entry, in vt7_orsini_record, dates his tenure of the title 1950-1958).

vt7_audit.topic: Audit corrections: Bracciano transfers; Martin V election date

claims.text: Flavio Orsini sold Bracciano and the ducal title to the Odescalchi in 1696; in 1803 the Torlonia family bought the ducal title and the castle; later the Odescalchi bought them back (no year given). The Torlonia family article instead says Pius VI created Giovanni Torlonia duke of Bracciano in 1794.
Martin V was elected pope on 11 November 1417 and died in Rome on 20 February 1431.
